priceSnapshot.note: OVERNIGHT DELIVERED THE MOVE ENDDAY WARNED ABOUT, AND IT WENT DOWN. Endday snapshotted 64,763.2 at 19:30 COT with an explicit warning: the base case was a quiet range, but if Asia opened and the dollar simply stopped falling, the one prop under this level went away. That is exactly what happened, with a fake-out first. At 20:00 COT price spiked to 65,388.0 - the highest print since Jul 29 and a clean break of the 65,152 momentum trigger endday had set - and then failed inside a single 15m candle, giving the whole move back and more. From that 65,388.0 high to the 64,026.1 low four and a half hours later is -2.08%, and price has spent the last three hours crawling sideways along the lows. Net against the endday snapshot: -1.10%. The 65,388.0 spike matters more than the drop, because it means the upside momentum trigger fired, found no follow-through at all, and reversed - the single most reliable bear signal this range produces, and the third failed break in three sessions. Underneath, four things changed and all four point the same way. FIRST, spot is now below EVERY short- and medium-term EMA on every timeframe except the 4H EMA200: below the 15m 20/50/100/200, below the 1H 20/50/100/200, below the 4H 20/50/100, and 861 dollars below the daily EMA50 that rejected it twice yesterday. Endday could still write that the 4H structure was intact with price above all four EMAs; that sentence is no longer true. SECOND, the dollar reversed. DXY is back at 100.22, +0.36% and back ABOVE the round number it broke on Thursday, so the six-week-low-dollar tailwind that midday and endday both leaned on has been given back inside one session. THIRD, the liquidity map inverted harder than at any point this week - see levels.liquidationMagnet. FOURTH, the equity non-confirmation got worse, not better: Nasdaq futures are +1.18% overnight and BTC is down 1.10% over the same hours. The one genuinely constructive fact in the whole report is that the Bitcoin ETF tape for Jul 30 finally published at +$233.1M net, the largest single-day inflow since the July drawdown began - institutions bought the day BTC refused to rally, and price has fallen since anyway.

reduceIf.confirmation: The STRUCTURAL rail is unchanged for a ninth consecutive session and has still never fired: a 4H CLOSE below $63,000 is what confirms the range break and takes the spot core down a real notch. The lowest print in that entire window is 62,684 and the lowest tonight is 64,026.1, so nothing has come close. What HAS changed is the live, non-structural line, and it has moved a long way: it is now $64,456, the 4H EMA50, with the 4H EMA20 at $64,340 just under it. Those two were support at the endday report and are resistance now. A 4H close back above $64,456 cancels the bearish tilt in this report outright; until then every bounce is a retest from below. Note that the net-exposure reduction for this session has ALREADY been taken, as a small futures hedge rather than another spot sale - this rail governs the next SPOT trim, not the hedge just executed.

addIf.confirmation: The add level moves DOWN from endday's $64,324 to $63,611, and it is the best-evidenced level in this report because three independent things land on it. First, the 4H EMA200 computed here sits at 63,610.66 - the last moving average of any timeframe still underneath spot, and therefore the last one that can act as support rather than resistance. Second, 63,611.0 was the exact low of the completed 2026-07-30 UTC daily candle, so it is a tested, defended price and not a theoretical one. Third, it sits just under the 63,888.6 liquidation shelf, which is where a flush would be aimed and where it would run out of fuel. The cash reserved from endday's trim goes here, and only on a 1H CLOSE that holds above it - not on the wick. The separate momentum tranche has been RESET UPWARD and hardened: after tonight's 65,388.0 failure, no long is taken on a break of the old 65,152 trigger; it now takes a 4H CLOSE above $65,388 to earn one.

decisionBox.changed: Stance stays REDUCE, bias tilt stays bearish, confidence rises 5.50 -> 6.00 and probabilities move 28/45/27 -> 23/44/33. Confidence goes UP on a bearish call because the endday thesis was tested overnight and confirmed rather than merely repeated. Four specific changes since 19:30 COT. (1) THE UPSIDE TRIGGER FIRED AND FAILED. Endday named a 4H close above 65,152 as the momentum tranche. Price printed 65,388.0 at 20:00 COT, took the level, held it for under fifteen minutes and reversed 2.08% into the 64,026.1 low. A trigger that fires and immediately fails is worse information than one that never fires. (2) THE EMA STACK BROKE. At the endday report spot was above the 4H EMA20 (64,431), EMA50 (64,494), EMA100 (64,384) and EMA200 (63,968). It is now below the first three - 4H EMA20 64,339.56, EMA50 64,455.93, EMA100 64,357.24 - and the only support left is the EMA200 at 63,610.66. On the 1H and 15m it is below all four. (3) THE DOLLAR PROP REVERSED. DXY 99.999 -> 100.22, +0.36% and back above the round number. Endday listed this as the first of four overnight risks and it landed. (4) THE MAGNET GOT HEAVIER AND CLOSER. The dominant band is now $63,888.6 at a 414-percent-larger leverage reading than the nearest band above, and it sits 0.25% below spot instead of 0.68%. Against all of that, two honest counterweights that stop this becoming a full bearish call: the Jul 30 ETF tape published at +$233.1M net inflow, the largest since the drawdown started, and the 4H MACD histogram is still positive at +58.23. That is why the tilt is bearish and the bias is still range.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is DOWN and it is the most lopsided reading of the week. The band immediately below spot carries a 873.97K leverage figure against 334.22K immediately above - a 162% skew - and the downside band is also closer, 0.25% away versus 1.09%. Between spot and the upside band there is a measured DEAD ZONE: the sample at 64,391.9 returned a leverage reading of exactly 0, meaning there is nothing at all to slow a bounce until 64,751 and nothing to catch a fall until 63,888. Two honest qualifications. First, the 24h long/short split is 50.16%/49.84%, a ratio of 1.01 - as neutral as this gauge gets, and a continuation of the de-crowding from 1.81 three days ago. There is no trapped-long overhang left to cascade, so the magnet is a target rather than a trigger. Second, open interest is flat on the day (-0.01% at $112.0B) while 24h liquidations fell a further 21.12% to $217.3M. Positions are neither being added nor flushed. That describes a coiled, low-conviction book, and a book like that tends to get dragged toward whichever shelf is heaviest - which is the one below.

atr.source: Computed here (Wilder ATR-14) from Kraken XBTUSDT daily OHLC over 38 sessions through the in-progress 2026-07-31 UTC candle, seeded on a 14-bar simple average of true range starting 2026-06-24 and then Wilder-smoothed for 24 further bars. Math: TR = max(H-L, |H-Cprev|, |L-Cprev|), then ATR = (ATRprev x 13 + TR) / 14. ATR has EXPANDED from endday's 1,505.83 to 1,601.65 (+6.4%) and the reason is tonight specifically: the in-progress daily candle has already covered 65,388.0 - 64,026.1 = $1,362 in nineteen hours, against a completed 2026-07-30 range of $1,541. At 2.50% of spot a normal day now covers about $1,602, which is the arithmetic behind leaving the resting stop at 63,200 - that is $850 below spot, roughly half an ATR, and it sits below both the 63,611 confluence and the 63,385 shelf so a normal night cannot reach it.

scalpContext.intradayBias: Bearish but late. The overnight box is 64,026.1 to 65,388.0, and price has spent the last three hours pinned in the bottom eighth of it. The compressed 1H EMA band at 64,369-64,567 is the ceiling and the 63,888.6 shelf is the floor, with a measured dead zone between spot and 64,751 that means a bounce would travel fast and stop hard. Long only above a 15m close over 64,340 with 64,456 as the first real gate; short only below a 15m close under 64,026 with 63,889 as the first target and 63,611 as the second. Between those two lines there is no edge worth paying spread for, and with 15m RSI at 33.85 the short side is the crowded one right now.

etfFlows.note: THE BEST NEWS IN THE REPORT, AND IT ARRIVED LATE. Farside's daily Bitcoin ETF table was blank for 30 Jul at the endday run three and a half hours after the US close; it has now published, and the number is large: +$233.1M NET INFLOW, made up of IBIT +183.4, BITB +20.7, FBTC +15.5, MSBT +7.4, HODL +2.3, BTC +2.3 and ARKB +1.5, with no fund printing an outflow. That is the biggest single-day inflow since this drawdown began and it follows Jul 29's +$32.1M, so streakDays counts 2 consecutive inflow days after a four-session run of -$225.1M, -$240.1M, -$11.6M and -$49.7M. Put it in scale honestly: +$233.1M against a lifetime daily average of +$80.6M is a strong day, roughly 2.9x normal, though still a sixth of the +$1,373.8M lifetime maximum. The uncomfortable reading is the one that matters for tonight: institutions bought $233M of Bitcoin on the exact session when spot refused to rally on a six-week-low dollar and a +3.70% Nasdaq-100, and price is 1.10% LOWER since. When a large, price-insensitive bid shows up and the tape still cannot hold, the marginal seller is bigger than the marginal buyer. On the flows-adjacent side: DXY has REVERSED back through 100 to 100.22 (+0.36%) as of 01:20 COT, undoing Thursday's break; Brent is 87.80 (-1.38%) and Nasdaq futures are +1.18% at 28,570 with S&P futures +0.49% and VIX 17.09 - the equity risk bid is still on and BTC is still not taking it.

calibration.note: actingHelped is TRUE, and it is the first honest yes in three sessions. Endday moved the stance to REDUCE at 64,763.2, trimmed roughly a tenth of the spot core, set a resting stop at 63,200 and wrote out four specific overnight risks. Spot is now 64,050.0, so the trim is +1.10% better than holding, the stop was never approached, and the FIRST of the four named risks - 'if Asia opens and the dollar simply stops falling, the one prop under this level goes away' - is exactly what happened, with DXY back through 100 to 100.22. priorReduceFired is FALSE: the 63,000 structural rail was never approached, so the REDUCE that helped was the discretionary one, not the rail. Two further calibration points. A MISS worth logging: endday's addIf level was $64,324, and price went straight through it at 21:00 COT without pausing - the 414.25K band that justified it did not hold, which is a useful reminder that a heatmap shelf is a target, not a floor, and that 'add on a 1H close above it' was the right qualifier even though the level was wrong. A HIT: endday's momentum trigger at a 4H close above 65,152 was set deliberately at the day's actual high rather than a round number, and tonight's 65,388.0 spike failed to produce that close - the qualifier saved a chase into a 2.08% reversal. Three sessions running, the level-setting has been better than the direction-setting.
